title: Macrocyclic diterpenoids from Stellera chamaejasme roots alleviate imiquimod-induced psoriasiform inflammation via STAT1/S100A9 signalling pathway.
authors: Nie, Yi-Wen; Liu, Xin; Peng, Ying; Zhang, Chun-Yan; Xi, Ruo-Fan; Jiang, Xiao-Xue; Wang, Yi; Lu, Han-Zhi; Guo, Dong-Jie; Guo, Wan-Jun; Duan, Yan-Juan; Nian, Hua; Wang, Kou; Chen, Jian-Yu; Li, Fu-Lun; Zhu, Jian-Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然产物SA通过STAT1/S100A9通路缓解银屑病炎症，虽含分子对接但核心是药物-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Psoriasis is a multisystem inflammatory disease with a significant impact on quality of life. Stellera chamaejasme, a medicinal plant used in traditional Chinese medicine, shows promise for the treatment of psoriasis. We identified diterpenoids in S. chamaejasme, including a new compound, stellchamain A (SA, 1), with notable antipsoriasis properties. This study explored the effects of SA on psoriasis to determine the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic efficacy of S. chamaejasme. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Compounds isolated by column chromatography were structurally identified using NMR spectroscopy. The effects of SA on IL-17A-treated HaCaT cell viability and apoptosis were assessed using CCK-8 and TUNEL assays. In vivo anti-psoriasis activity of SA was evaluated in a mouse model of imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis. Network pharmacology, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were elucidated the interactions between SA and the targets. KEY RESULTS: SA was isolated from S. chamaejasme along with nine known analogues (2-10). In vivo, SA reduced IMQ-induced epidermal thickness, hyperkeratosis, and perivascular inflammatory cell infiltration. Network pharmacology indicated that SA may function via the interleukin IL-17A/STAT1/S100A9 pathway. The results of SPR assays and molecular docking showed that SA binds to STAT1 with a K(D) value of 9.24 nM. DARTS and CETSA analyses confirmed a direct and relevant interaction between SA and STAT1. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: SA modulates the immunological microenvironment to treat psoriasis by targeting the IL-17A/STAT1/S100A9 axis, representing a potential new treatment for psoriasis and other IL-17A-mediated skin disorders.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：银屑病是一种多系统炎症性疾病，对生活质量有显著影响。瑞香狼毒（Stellera chamaejasme）是一种用于传统中药的药用植物，在银屑病治疗方面显示出潜力。我们从瑞香狼毒中鉴定出二萜类化合物，包括一种新化合物stellchamain A（SA，1），具有显著的抗银屑病特性。本研究探讨了SA对银屑病的作用，以确定瑞香狼毒治疗效果的潜在机制。实验方法：通过柱色谱分离的化合物使用核磁共振波谱进行结构鉴定。使用CCK-8和TUNEL实验评估SA对IL-17A处理的HaCaT细胞活力和凋亡的影响。在咪喹莫特（IMQ）诱导的银屑病小鼠模型中评估了SA的体内抗银屑病活性。通过网络药理学、表面等离子体共振（SPR）、药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）和细胞热位移实验（CETSA）阐明了SA与靶标之间的相互作用。关键结果：从瑞香狼毒中分离出SA及九种已知类似物（2-10）。在体内，SA减少了IMQ诱导的表皮厚度、角化过度和血管周围炎症细胞浸润。网络药理学表明SA可能通过白细胞介素IL-17A/STAT1/S100A9通路发挥作用。SPR实验和分子对接结果表明SA与STAT1结合，K(D)值为9.24 nM。DARTS和CETSA分析确认了SA与STAT1之间的直接且相关相互作用。结论与意义：SA通过靶向IL-17A/STAT1/S100A9轴调节免疫微环境以治疗银屑病，代表了银屑病及其他IL-17A介导的皮肤疾病的潜在新疗法。
